title: Fleet Controls: Scaling Orchestration Wizard and Throughput Chronicle
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a guided orchestration wizard in Console for fleet operators to define scaling policies, guaranteed throughput reservations, burst windows, and safe rollouts. Add a correlated throughput chronicle (timeline + per-change impact) that surfaces live and historical throughput, request-latency percentiles, and model-variant routing for each fleet. Goal: reduce operator error, shorten time-to-configure fleets, and improve post-change troubleshooting for Dedicated customers.

Background: Operators currently use a mix of manual API calls and disparate dashboards to change scaling presets. This leads to inconsistent guardrails across fleets, unexpected cost spikes, and lengthy incident post-mortems. The wizard + chronicle will codify best-practices (min/max capacity, cooldowns, budget caps, fallback models) and provide one-click rollbacks with annotated change history.

Scope: Console UI flows, server-side validation, audit events, telemetry for throughput/latency, migration adapter for existing presets, and a compact onboarding micro-UX for new operators. Not in scope: new autoscaler implementation (handled by ENG-51234) and billing integration (separate PM).

Acceptance criteria:
- Wizard: step-based flow with templates (latency-first, cost-first, balanced) and fields: min/max replicas, reserved throughput units, burst allowance, cooldown window, model-variant fallback list, and canary percentage.
- Validation: client-side and server-side checks with clear error states and suggested corrections.
- Chronicle: time-series view of throughput (QPS and tokens/s), p50/p95 latency, autoscale decisions, and annotated change events (who, what, why).
- One-click rollback to previous scaling manifest with explanation of differences.
- Audit records emitted to the existing audit system and visible in fleet change history.
- Unit/e2e tests covering wizard forms, validation, and API wiring.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Users create overly aggressive scaling rules that cause cost overruns. Mitigation: add budget caps, warning modalities, and a default "cost guardrail" template.
- Risk: Data latency in chronicle leads to wrong operator conclusions. Mitigation: display data staleness, and add a live tail mode for recent 5m window.

Open questions:
- Should the wizard enforce supplier-specific kernel/quantization compatibility for fallback model variants? (Design + Eng to decide)
- What is the default canary rollout cadence (10% for 15m vs 5% for 30m)?

Related artifacts: Figma mockups (see attachments), PRD in Confluence, telemetry schema in docs, staging dashboard link.
